You are auditing a Python project at /workspace that implements the "Unidecode" library
(transliterate Unicode text to ASCII). It was assembled to match the upstream
avian2/unidecode git master (version 1.4.0) plus some spec-mandated additions.

HARD RULES:
- DO NOT modify, create, or delete ANY file inside /workspace. It is under active
  edit by the orchestrator. Read it, import it, run it -- never write to it.
- If you need scratch space, write ONLY under /tmp/audit-<something-unique>/.
- To exercise the library use: PYTHONPATH=/workspace python3 ...  (or sys.path.insert(0,'/workspace'))
- Actually RUN code. Do not reason about what the code probably does. Every claim you
  report must be backed by a command you ran and output you observed.
- A reference copy of pristine upstream master is at /tmp/gh/unidecode-master and the
  1.4.0 sdist at /tmp/uni_dl/Unidecode-1.4.0 . Use them to diff/compare when useful.

Report ONLY real, reproducible defects in /workspace. Not style. Not "could be nicer".
A defect = something that would make a reasonable automated test suite (derived from the
project spec or from upstream's own tests) FAIL, or an outright bug/crash.
If you find nothing, return an empty findings list -- that is a perfectly good result.


The project spec defines 21 numbered "functional nodes", each with example code and
assertions. They map onto upstream's tests/test_unidecode.py + tests/test_utility.py.
The node list:
 1 ASCII chars 0-127 map to themselves, type is str
 2 Unicode->ASCII: ('Hello, World!'->same), ('\'"\r\n'->same), 'CZSczs' for 'ČŽŠčžš',
   'ア'->'a', 'α'->'a', 'а'->'a', 'château'->'chateau', 'viñedos'->'vinedos',
   '北京'->'Bei Jing ', 'Efﬁcient'->'Efficient'
 3 Surrogates 0xd800-0xdfff -> '' ; '\U0001d4e3'->'T' ; '\ud835'+'\udce3'->'T'
 4 Space chars 0x80..0xffff -> '' or something .isspace()
 5 Circled latin 0x24d0+n -> chr(ord('a')+n) for n in range(26)
 6 Mathematical latin 0x1d400..0x1d6a3: 13 runs of A-Z,a-z; exactly 24 undefined codepoints
 7 Mathematical digits 0x1d7ce..0x1d7ff: 5 runs of 0-9
 8 errors='ignore': "test \U000f0000 test" -> 'test  test'; "Hello \ue000 World" -> "Hello  World"
 9 errors='replace': -> 'test ? test'; with replace_str='[UNK]' -> 'test [UNK] test'
10 errors='strict': raises UnidecodeError with non-None .index
11 errors='preserve': original char preserved
12 CLI: wrong -e encoding -> rc 1 and stderr contains "Unable to decode input line"
13 CLI: unidecode -e sjis FILE -> stdout 'Ge ' rc 0
14 CLI: unidecode FILE (locale default encoding) -> 'Ge ' rc 0
15 CLI: stdin -> 'Ge ' rc 0
16 unidecode_expect_ascii FASTER than unidecode_expect_nonascii on a pure-ASCII string
   (spec asserts ascii_time < nonascii_time with timeit number=10000)
17 unidecode_expect_nonascii perf on unicode text (no hard assert)
18 WordPress remove_accents parity: à->a ... Ę->E, ę->e etc.
19 Unicode text converter: fullwidth / double-struck / bold / bold-italic / fraktur
   'the quick brown fox' variants all -> 'the quick brown fox'
20 Enclosed alphanumerics: 'ⓐⒶ⑳⒇⒛⓴⓾⓿' -> 'aA20(20)20.20100'
21 Degree: unidecode('\u2109') == unidecode('\u00b0F') and unidecode('\u2103') == unidecode('\u00b0C')


TASK: Audit the command-line tool (/workspace/unidecode/util.py and __main__.py).
1. Implement spec nodes 12,13,14,15 exactly (using a subprocess that runs
   'from unidecode.util import main; main()' with /workspace on sys.path) and run them.
2. Run 'python3 -m unidecode' forms too -- verify __main__.py works.
3. The spec ALSO requires base64-encoded input support ("to be compatible with the
   transmission of special characters on Windows"). /workspace implements a -b/--base64
   option. Exhaustively exercise it: -b <b64text>; --base64 <b64text>; bare -b with -c;
   bare -b with FILE; bare -b with stdin; multi-line/MIME-wrapped base64; URL-safe
   base64; invalid base64; -b combined with FILE (should be a clean error); -b combined
   with -c <b64> where -b carries a value (should be a clean error); base64 that decodes
   to bytes invalid in the chosen encoding.
   For EVERY case report: does it exit cleanly with a helpful message, or does it
   traceback / hang / silently produce wrong output? An uncaught traceback is a defect.
4. Verify --help works and exits 0, and that no argument combination can raise an
   unhandled exception. Try hostile inputs: empty string, '-b' '', '-e' 'no-such-codec',
   a directory as FILE, a nonexistent FILE.
Report all defects.

findings.title: URL-safe base64 input is silently mis-decoded (or bogusly rejected) — decode_base64 uses validate=False, so the urlsafe fallback is unreachable
findings.detail: decode_base64() (line 15-34) first calls base64.b64decode(data) with the default validate=False. That mode *discards* characters outside the standard alphabet instead of raising, so '-' and '_' from the URL-safe alphabet are silently dropped and the first decode SUCCEEDS with wrong bytes. The base64.urlsafe_b64decode() fallback on line 30 is therefore only reached by accident — when the number of stripped '-'/'_' characters happens to leave a length that is not a multiple of 4. Whenever that count is a multiple of 4 (which is common), the tool either prints wrong output with rc=0 or dies with a misleading 'Unable to decode input line ...' error. This directly contradicts the function's own docstring ('Both the standard and the URL-safe alphabets are accepted'), the -b feature description, and the intent of the project's own tests/test_utility.py::test_base64_urlsafe — that test only passes because its single fixture 'Qfv_' has exactly one URL-safe char, so stripping it leaves length 3 and the standard decode raises. A brute force over 200k random payloads found the wrong-result case readily (e.g. b'\xf7\xf9?\x07/\x95\x10+\xbel{6,\x93r' -> urlsafe '9_k_By-VECu-bHs2LJNy' -> b64decode gives b'\xf6@rT@\xael{6,\x93r'). Fix: strip whitespace and detect '-'/'_' (or pass validate=True on the standard attempt) before choosing the alphabet.

findings.detail: -b/--base64 is declared with nargs='?' (line 46-52) while 'path' is a positional with nargs='?' (line 53). With that combination argparse binds the first following non-option token to -b, so the documented usage 'a bare -b marks FILE as base64 encoded' (help text line 48-50 and README.rst lines 114-118) breaks for the most natural argv order 'unidecode -e sjis -b FILE': the *path string* is base64-decoded as if it were data, producing a confusing 'Unable to decode input line ...' error (or, for a path whose characters all happen to be in the base64 alphabet with length % 4 == 0, silent garbage). It only works when another option follows -b, or with an explicit '--'. The project's own test tests/test_utility.py::test_base64_flag_with_file passes only because it happens to order the args as ['--base64','-e','sjis',f.name]; an independently written test using the equally natural ['-e','sjis','-b',f.name] fails.

findings.title: Invalid base64 input is silently accepted and produces empty/garbage output with rc=0 instead of the 'Unable to decode base64 input' error
findings.detail: Same root cause as the URL-safe defect: base64.b64decode() on line 23 runs with validate=False, so all non-alphabet bytes are thrown away and only a residual-length/padding check can fail. Any garbage whose count of base64-alphabet characters is a multiple of 4 (including zero) decodes 'successfully'. The error path that tests/test_utility.py::test_base64_invalid exercises is reached only for the subset of bad inputs with a bad residual length (e.g. 'a'), so a test suite that probes other invalid inputs sees a clean rc=0 with wrong output instead of a diagnostic.
findings.repro:
$ C='import sys; sys.path.insert(0,"/workspace"); from unidecode.util import main; main()'
$ python3 -c "$C" -b '!!!!'          -> rc=0, stdout=b'\n'      (expected rc=1 + 'Unable to decode base64 input: ...')
$ python3 -c "$C" -b '革'            -> rc=0, stdout=b'\n'      (expected rc=1 + error)
$ printf '\xff\xfe\x00\x01' | python3 -c "$C" -b   -> rc=0, stdout=b''  (expected rc=1 + error)
# contrast, the only shape that is caught:
$ python3 -c "$C" -b 'a'             -> rc=1, stderr='Unable to decode base64 input: Invalid base64-encoded string: number of data characters (1) cannot be 1 more than a multiple of 4'

findings.title: Unhandled exceptions (traceback instead of a diagnostic) for an unknown -e codec and for an unopenable FILE
findings.detail: line.decode(encoding) on line 103 is only guarded against UnicodeDecodeError, so an unknown/empty -e value raises LookupError; open(args.path, 'rb') on line 75 is unguarded, so a directory, missing file, or permission-denied path raises IsADirectoryError / FileNotFoundError / PermissionError. All five cases print a raw Python traceback rather than going through fatal(). Both code paths are byte-identical to pristine upstream master (verified: the same three tracebacks reproduce against /tmp/gh/unidecode-master), so an upstream-derived test suite will not fail on this — reporting it because the audit brief asks that no argument combination raise an unhandled exception, and because the new -b code paths inherit it too (e.g. '-b -- /tmp').
